result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. Registration takes them, `updateSupplier` changes them, and all four listings and the single lookup return them. The full offline suite passes (609 tests, including two new ones in `SupplierTest`). Nothing is committed.

- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. The existing 5-argument constructor defaults it to 30 (`DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS`), so the ~100 existing call sites compile unchanged.
- **`src/main/resources/schema.sql`**: `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CHECK (payment_terms_days >= 0)` on `supplier`.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the column. `listSuppliersOrderedByName`, `listSuppliersInCountry`, `listSuppliersWithRatingAtLeast` and `findSupplierById` read it. I also added it to the other queries that build a `Supplier` (reorder suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, performance, spending, single-supplier-per-category), so those objects don't silently show 30.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: tests that 45 days registered and renegotiated to 14 shows 14 in every listing, and that an unspecified supplier gets 30.

The repo has no UI layer, so "entering" terms means passing them to `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier`. I did not change the demo output in `DemoScenario`.
